messages:
incident-bot: PAGER — GPU pool 'dedicated-usw2-42' reporting sustained saturation >95% and request queue growth >1200. autoscaler attempted 3 scale ops and hit quota. severity: P1.
Jordan: ack, I'm awake. seeing alerts in console.
Maya: noticed increased tail latency on /v1/generate around 15:02 UTC, error 429s from router when queue > 1000.
Sahil: loading recent rollout notes — v10.0.3 changed kv-window management by increasing retention for KV entries (longer context lifecycle). could be KV working set blowup.
Priya: tentative customer impact: a handful of high-throughput customers using long-context modes started getting throttles and some timed-out requests. CS told Olivia-CS about degraded perf.
Olivia-CS: Customer report from AcornAI and FinSight — heavy timeouts for long-chat sessions. they're seeing errors in the app. asking for ETA.
Jordan: timeline — rollout v10.0.3 deployed 14:40 UTC to dedicated pools via canary -> 100%. deploy-bot shows no errors during rollout.
deploy-bot: deploy v10.0.3 completed 14:52 UTC across dedicated pools.
Greg-Infra: checking autoscaler logs — "scale attempt rejected: quota_exceeded: reserved_capacity_limit". looks like we hit committed-reserved and cannot request more instances.
Runtime-Team: heap/kv-metrics show KV index size per worker jumped ~3.6x after v10.0.3; per-GPU memory pressure up, resulting in slower inference and lower throughput per GPU.
Jordan: immediate mitigations: 1) throttle long-context routes, 2) enable fallback routing to v9 variant (lower retention), 3) attempt manual capacity increase from infra console if allowed, 4) alert customers.
Maya: putting short rules in router now to block context > 8k for affected customers and return 429 with guidance. doing a canary at 15:20 UTC.
Sahil: putting this command to reduce KV retention window on the active model config (temporary):
```
redwood model update-config v10.0.3 --kv-window=2m --eviction=aggressive
```
Will that take effect without restart? runtime says it supports hot-config for kv-window.
Runtime-Team: confirmed: kv-window is hot-configurable but eviction will take one full cycle to reclaim. could reduce working set after ~2-3 minutes.
Greg-Infra: manual capacity increase request to cloud team submitted (ticket #INC-9481). however reserved_capacity_limit is in our contract; cloud needs approval for burst.
Jordan: starting controlled fallback: route 30% of traffic to v9.9 variant for customers with high throughput. Config snippet: 
```
routing set policy rollouts:v9.9 fallback if: pool_util>85% && queue_len>400
```
Maya: routing patch applied at 15:26 UTC. Initial metrics: queue dropped ~18% in 3m for the canary.
Priya: CS notified AcornAI + FinSight that we're throttling long contexts temporarily and routing to fallback. gave them 30m window estimate.
Olivia-CS: they asked for more concrete ETA; I told them we expect stabilization in 10-20m while we scale and backfill.
Runtime-Team: after kv-window change and fallback, KV working set decreased ~28% in affected workers. per-GPU throughput improved ~12% but still below baseline.
Jordan: autoscaler still failing to request instances due to quota. need ops help to unblock quota or do manual preemption.
Greg-Infra: update — cloud granted emergency burst capacity of 6 GPUs, available in ~9 minutes. ramping those into pool now.
incident-bot: NOTE: schedule shift — Jordan to hand off to next oncall at 16:00 UTC.
Jordan: I'll stay until autoscaler healthy or we fully roll back. handing to Greg at 16:00 if unresolved.
Sahil: root cause hypothesis: v10.0.3 changed KV retention semantics and inadvertently increased KV index lifespan + indexing granularity. high throughput customers with long contexts caused working set to grow beyond per-GPU memory, lowering tokens/sec and forcing queue to grow. autoscaler configuration expected throughput per-GPU, but the degraded throughput meant we hit reservation limits and then quota prevented additional nodes.
Priya: customers impacted: AcornAI (realtime chat), FinSight (batch summarization), BetaLabs (small fraction). severity: degraded performance, some 429/timeout errors.
Maya: rollback option: revert to v9.9. Pros: immediate return of baseline KV footprint. Cons: loses v10 improvements for other customers. Recommendation: keep fallback routing for heavy sessions and roll v10 back in staging while we tune kv-window.
Greg-Infra: emergency GPUs are live at 15:41 UTC. pool util dropped to 76%, queue decreased to ~240. throttles reduced.
Jordan: good. now: 1) keep throttles for long contexts for 30m, 2) maintain fallback routing at 30% for heavy customers, 3) open follow-up to adjust autoscaler to be throughput-aware (not just util), 4) schedule rollback if we can't stabilize.
Sahil: creating post-incident ticket with action items: fix KV retention defaults, add regression test for kv-index memory, update canary criteria to include per-GPU tokens/sec, and add autoscaler safeguards to request emergency burst earlier.
Maya: pushing a short announcement to #status with guidance for affected customers. Olivia-CS: please coordinate customer comms.
Olivia-CS: messaging sent to AcornAI and FinSight at 15:55 UTC — described mitigations and offered dedicated follow-up call.
Jordan: handoff to Greg-Infra at 16:00 UTC. Greg, please pick up timeline and confirm next steps for rollback or tuning.
Greg-Infra: acked. will continue incident lead. current status: pool stabilized with emergency GPUs, KV working set trending down, autoscaler still disabled for bursts until quota approved permanently. investigating why canary didn't catch kv-index growth.
incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE — severity downgraded to P2 at 16:12 UTC, customer-visible throttles largely mitigated, follow-up required.
Jordan: thanks team. open action items to triage tomorrow: detailed memory allocation traces for v10, backport hotfix for kv eviction, autoscaler policy changes, and update runbooks.
Sahil: adding timeline/metrics to postmortem draft.
Olivia-CS: I'll gather customer impact logs and support tickets for retro.
Greg-Infra: leaving notes for next shift in the incident doc: emergency GPUs returned to pool at 17:10 after autoscaler config and quota changes.
Runtime-Team: leaving logs snippet for engineers: 
```
[15:18:43] worker-42 kv_index_entries=8.3M memory=14.9G tokens/sec=180
[15:21:12] worker-42 kv_index_entries=31.2M memory=23.8G tokens/sec=52
```
Jordan: closing active paging and marking incident as stabilized. will publish full postmortem once follow-ups complete. :thumbsup:
